mainTopic: Two topics: how a man's wording decides whether several small קידושין items add up (רבא), and רב's rule that קידושין with a loan does not work.
overview: רבא limits the משנה's case of a woman eating the dates. If the man said 'with this, and with this, and with this,' each item is a separate gift, so items she eats do not add up. If he said 'with these,' all the items are one package and already hers, so they add up even if she eats them. The גמרא first works out that the ברייתא's case of 'an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut' means 'with these.' It then proves רבא from that ברייתא. Next it asks how רב and שמואל can explain the ברייתא, and answers that it follows רבי, who counts items named one by one as separate. A new topic begins: רב rules that קידושין with a loan does not work, because a loan is given to be spent. The גמרא shows that a ברייתא with a dispute on this is really about a promised מנה that was one דינר short, and explains why רבי אלעזר's ruling fits everyone. Finally, a ברייתא is brought that seems to say קידושין with a loan does work, challenging רב, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא limits the משנה's case of eating the dates
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה's ruling, that dates she ate do not count together, applies only when he said 'with this, and with this, and with this.' If he said 'with these,' they count together even if she eats them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's rule applies only where he said to her 'With this, and with this, and with this.' But if he said 'With these,' she is betrothed even while eating them, because when she eats, she is eating her own food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains exactly when the משנה's rule about a woman eating the dates applies. The key is the man's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'with this, and with this' makes each date its own separate קידושין gift, so a date she already ate cannot join the later ones. Saying 'with these' makes all of them one gift. Once she accepts that package, the dates are already hers, so eating them does not cancel anything.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when; a phrase that limits an earlier ruling to a specific case
With this, and with this, and with this; each item is offered separately
With these; all the items are offered as one package
From her own; the food already belongs to her

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole rest of the passage. The difference between 'with these' and 'with this, and with this' is what the ברייתא and the questions that follow will turn on.

phrases.english: They only taught this where he said to her:
phrases.notes: This is רבא speaking, about the משנה's case where she ate the dates one at a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's ruling about the dates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'this, and this, and this,' eaten items do not combine. With 'these,' they combine even if she eats them, because they are already hers.

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits רבא's distinction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists several wordings. It mentions the problem of eating the items only in the 'with this, and with this' case, which matches רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רבא. If he said 'Be betrothed to me with an acorn, a pomegranate and a nut,' or 'with these,' she is betrothed if all of them together are worth a פרוטה, and not otherwise. If he said 'with this, and with this, and with this,' she is betrothed if all together are worth a פרוטה, and not otherwise. If he said 'with this' and she took it and ate it, then 'with this' and she ate it, and so on, she is not betrothed unless one single item is worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבא. It lists three wordings and their rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'these' and 'this, and this, and this' combine when nothing is eaten. Only the 'this, and this' wording loses its combining power once she eats the items one by one. That is exactly רבא's distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him
An acorn, the fruit of an oak tree; a very cheap item
Worth a פרוטה, the minimum value needed for קידושין
She took it and ate it

steps.confusionAlert: Both 'these' and 'this, and this, and this' can add up to a פרוטה. The difference shows up only when she eats the items one at a time.

steps.title: What does the first case of the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact wording the ברייתא's first case, 'with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut,' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case of 'with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut': what situation is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's first case. This sets up the next steps, which test possible meanings one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut' is unclear. It could mean 'or,' 'and,' or 'these.' Pinning it down shows whether the ברייתא truly supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?

phrases.english: This case of "with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut":
what situation is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי בְּאַלּוֹן בְּרִמּוֹן בֶּאֱגוֹז הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the first clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording behind the ברייתא's first case.

steps.title: It cannot mean "or"
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'either an acorn, or a pomegranate, or a nut,' adding the items together would make no sense, because 'or' means only one item is the קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he told her 'either with an acorn, or with a pomegranate, or with a nut,' how could she be betrothed when all of them together are worth a פרוטה? He said 'or'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning, 'or,' and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Or' means only one single item is the קידושין. In that case that one item would need to be worth a פרוטה by itself. Yet the ברייתא lets the items add up, so 'or' cannot be the case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that is about to be tested
But look; introduces a challenge

phrases.english: If you say that he told her:
"Either with an acorn, or with a pomegranate, or with a nut,"

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בְּכוּלָּן שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת?
phrases.english: would she be betrothed if all of them together are worth a פרוטה?
But he said "or"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible meaning.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'or' reading of the first clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Or' points to one single item, so the items could not add up.

steps.title: It cannot mean "and"
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'with an acorn, and a pomegranate, and a nut,' that is the same as 'with this, and with this, and with this,' which the ברייתא already lists as its own case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if he said 'with an acorn, and with a pomegranate, and with a nut,' that is the same as 'with this, and with this, and with this'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second possible meaning, 'and,' and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming each item with 'and' is the same as 'this, and this, and this.' The ברייתא teaches that case separately later on. It would not teach the same case twice.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as; points out that two cases are identical

phrases.english: Rather, if he said "with an acorn, and with a pomegranate, and with a nut":
that is the same as "with this, and with this, and with this"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא בְּאַלּוֹן וּבְרִמּוֹן וּבֶאֱגוֹז הַיְינוּ בָּזוֹ וּבָזוֹ וּבָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second possible meaning after the first one failed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'and' reading of the first clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would repeat the later 'this, and this, and this' case.

steps.title: So it must mean "with these"
steps.stepSummary: Since 'or' and 'and' both fail, the גמרא suggests the case is where he said 'with these.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a case where he said to her 'with these'?
steps.whatsHappening: With the other two options ruled out, the גמרא proposes the remaining one: he said 'with these.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading fits the rule that the items add up. It also keeps 'these' apart from 'this, and this,' which matches רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? Proposes the remaining option

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it a case where he said to her "with these"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the remaining reading after the other two were rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first clause is a case where he said 'with these.'

steps.title: But "with these" is listed as a separate case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to say 'or if he said: with these,' which shows that its first case is not 'with these.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the next part says 'or if he said to her: be betrothed to me with these,' that shows the first part is not talking about 'these'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just proposed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'or' in the ברייתא introduces 'with these' as a new case. That suggests the first case must be something different from 'with these.'

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching
This implies; a conclusion drawn from what the text says
We are dealing with

phrases.english: But since the later part teaches:
"Or if he said to her, 'Be betrothed to me with these'":
this implies that the first part is not dealing with "these."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'with these' reading proposed in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first clause means 'with these.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא adds 'with these' as an extra case with 'or,' so the first case must be different.

steps.title: The ברייתא is explaining its own first case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is not adding a new case. It is explaining the first case: 'with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut' means he said 'with these.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining itself: 'Be betrothed to me with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut.' How so? For example, where he said to her 'Be betrothed to me with these.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The 'with these' line explains the first case; it is not a separate one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's word 'or' should be read as 'that is to say.' So the first case really is 'with these,' and its rule is that the items add up. This stands next to the 'this, and this' case, where eating breaks them apart. That is just what רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining; the second line explains the first instead of adding a new case
How so? Introduces an explanation
For example, such as

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's first case, 'with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut,' is explained as 'with these.' Steps 9-10 use this reading to prove רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The careful reading saves the ברייתא as support for רבא. It also shows how the exact words a man uses decide whether קידושין takes effect.

phrases.english: It is explaining itself:
"Be betrothed to me with an acorn, a pomegranate, a nut."
How so?
For example, where he said to her, "Be betrothed to me with these."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7 and confirms the reading from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: the second line explains the first case instead of adding a new one.

steps.terutzMaskana: The first case is 'with these.' The next steps (9-10) use this reading to prove רבא from the ברייתא.

steps.title: The latter clause of the ברייתא treats a single item differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the latter clause of the ברייתא. When he said 'with this' and she ate it, the קידושין works only if one item alone is worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter clause of the ברייתא teaches: if he said 'with this,' and she took it and ate it, then if one of them is worth a פרוטה she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its proof by quoting the latter clause of the ברייתא. This is a setup: the next step will contrast it with the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the latter clause, each item is given on its own ('with this'), so each item must stand alone. If she eats one, the ברייתא makes a point of saying that a single item must be worth a פרוטה. The גמרא will now point out that the first clause has no such condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a teaching
'With this' (one single item)
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest value that can make קידושין
She is betrothed

phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches: 'With this'
she took it and ate it,

phrases.english: if one of them is worth a peruta, she is betrothed;
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that step 8 has shown the first clause means 'with these,' the גמרא brings the latter clause to build a contrast.
steps.raayaObject: That 'with these' lets the woman eat her own items without spoiling the קידושין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The latter clause of the ברייתא, where eating a single item requires that item alone to be worth a פרוטה.

steps.title: With 'with these,' she eats her own food
steps.stepSummary: The first clause makes no difference between eating and keeping the items. This proves that when he says 'with these,' her eating is eating her own food, and the קידושין stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first clause makes no difference between a woman who eats the items and one who keeps them. Learn from this: whenever he said 'with these,' when she eats, she is eating her own. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two clauses and draws its conclusion. In the 'with these' case, eating the items does not hurt the קידושין at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The latter clause ('with this') adds a special condition for eating, but the first clause ('with these') does not. So with 'with these' the items already belong to her as one group of קידושין. Her eating them is not a problem, and the statement of רבא is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a teaching
Makes a distinction
A woman who eats (the items)
A woman who sets aside (keeps) the items
From her own (property)
Learn from it (a conclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: When a man says 'with these,' all the items count together as one קידושין, and she may eat them as her own.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits well with רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא's latter clause fits the one who says the משנה's eating case is on its latter clause. That view reads 'one of them' as 'the last one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the eating case refers to the latter clause. He explains 'unless one of them is worth a פרוטה' as 'unless the last one is worth a פרוטה.' Here too, read it as 'unless the last one is worth a פרוטה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new problem. First it shows which view fits the ברייתא easily, to set up a question on the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי reads 'one of them' in the משנה as 'the last one.' The ברייתא's 'one of them' can be read the same way, so it fits him. The 'הניחא' formula signals that a challenge against another view is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (setting up a challenge to another view)
It refers to the latter clause
In the last one

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First it shows that the ברייתא fits רבי אמי smoothly, to highlight the difficulty for the other view.

steps.title: The problem for רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל say the eating case is on the first clause of the משנה. But the ברייתא lists items as one group, not one by one, so why would one item need to be worth a פרוטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב and שמואל, who both say the eating case refers to the first clause and that the eating case was needed, there is a problem. Here the ברייתא lists the items as a group; it does not list them one by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge against רב and שמואל. Their reading of the משנה does not seem to fit this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב and שמואל, 'one of them must be worth a פרוטה' is taught for separate items, each with its own 'be betrothed to me.' But in this ברייתא he says 'be betrothed to me' only once and lists the items as a group. So it is unclear why a single item would need to be worth a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: It refers to the first clause
It was necessary for him (to teach)

Individual items, each listed separately
Lists, counts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the משנה and the ברייתא. The 'first clause' and 'latter clause' in רב and שמואל's view and in רבי אמי's view are clauses of the משנה, which is now being tested against the ברייתא.

it refers to the first clause,
and the case of the woman eating was necessary for him to teach,
here it lists groupings,

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their reading needs separate items. The ברייתא gives a grouped statement yet still asks that one item be worth a פרוטה, which does not match.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי, who counts each item separately
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that needs one item worth a פרוטה follows רבי. He holds that listing items, with or without 'and', counts each one on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי. He says it makes no difference whether one says 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk' or 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk.' Either way, each item is counted on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 12. The ברייתא follows רבי, who treats a list of items as separate items, even according to רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 asked why one item alone must be worth a פרוטה if the items were listed as one group. The answer is that for רבי, naming items one after another, with or without 'and,' counts each item separately. So in the ברייתא's 'with this, and again with this' case, the eaten items do not add up, and one item must be worth a פרוטה on its own.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, listing items, even with the word 'and', still counts each item separately. That is why one item alone must be worth a פרוטה.

steps.title: רב: קידושין with a loan does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a man who is מקדש a woman with a loan he already gave her does not create קידושין, because loan money is given to be spent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If a man is מקדש a woman with a loan, she is not מקודשת, because a loan is given to be spent.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב states that forgiving a loan cannot serve as the money of קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a loan is given, the borrower may spend the money, so it already belongs to her. When the lender says 'be מקודשת with the loan,' he is not giving her anything new that is his.

keyTerms.meaning: a loan
it was given to be spent
betrothed, with קידושין in effect

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea 'a loan is given to be spent' drives the rest of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: רב said: One who betroths with a loan,
she is not betrothed,
since a loan is given to be spent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the eating case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with a loan does not work, because loan money is given to be spent.

steps.title: Is רב's rule a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא shows תנאים arguing about whether a loan is given to be spent, so רב would be taking one side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a dispute of תנאים? One taught: If a man is מקדש with a loan, she is not מקודשת. Some say: she is מקודשת. Isn't this their dispute: one holds a loan is given to be spent, and the other holds it is not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רב's rule is really one side of an argument between תנאים. This sets up the next move, where the suggestion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this reading is right, רב only agrees with the first opinion, and the יש אומרים disagree with him. The גמרא prefers not to leave רב on one side of a dispute, so it checks whether the ברייתא really says this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is a dispute of תנאים?
some say, a second opinion
Isn't it that...? It introduces a proposed reading
they disagree

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of תנאים?
One who betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed,
and some say: she is betrothed.
Isn't it that they disagree about this:
one holds a loan is given to be spent,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר מִלְוָה לָאו לְהוֹצָאָה נִיתְּנָה?
phrases.english: and the other holds a loan is not given to be spent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a תנאי dispute behind רב's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב's rule the subject of a dispute between תנאים in this ברייתא?

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא shows that is not the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says both sides agree that a sale made with a loan works. That could not be true if a loan is given to be spent, so the dispute must be about something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think so? Read the end of the ברייתא: 'And they agree about a sale, that he acquires.' If a loan is given to be spent, with what does he acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of Step 15. Both opinions in the ברייתא agree that a lender can buy something with the loan, so neither one can hold that a loan is given to be spent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If loan money already belongs to the borrower, the lender has nothing to buy with. Since both sides agree the sale works, both must hold that a loan is not given to be spent. So the argument about קידושין must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think so? A strong rejection
the later part of a source
a sale
With what does he acquire?

phrases.english: Do you really think so? Read the latter clause:
And they agree about a sale, that this one acquires.
phrases.notes: The lender buys something from the borrower in exchange for forgiving the loan.

phrases.english: If you say a loan is given to be spent,
with what does he acquire?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ברייתא's dispute is about whether a loan is given to be spent.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא has both sides agreeing that a sale with a loan works, which does not fit with 'a loan is given to be spent.'

steps.title: רב נחמן: the ברייתא is about a מנה missing one דינר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports that רב הונא reads the ברייתא as a different case: he promised her a מנה, and it turned out to be one דינר short.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Our colleague הונא explains it as other matters. What case are we dealing with? He said to her, 'Be מקודשת to me with a מנה,' and the מנה turned out to be one דינר short.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the ברייתא is not about a plain loan, רב נחמן gives the real case behind it. The missing דינר is like a loan he owes her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'loan' in the ברייתא is only the one missing דינר, which he now owes her. The question becomes whether he kept his word of 'a מנה,' not whether loan money can be used for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: our colleague
other matters, a different case
What case are we dealing with here?
a coin amount equal to one hundred דינרים
a דינר coin

phrases.english: רב נחמן said: Our colleague הונא
explains it as dealing with other matters,
and what are we dealing with here?
For example, where he said to her:
'Be betrothed to me with a מנה,'
and the מנה was found to be missing one דינר.
phrases.notes: That missing דינר is what the ברייתא calls a 'loan.' It is now money he owes her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הוּנָא חַבְרִין מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּמִילֵּי אוּחְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 16 rejected the first reading, this gives a new case for the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a plain loan and argues against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a promised מנה that was one דינר short, so it does not argue with רב.

steps.title: The argument: would she be too embarrassed to ask for the missing דינר?
steps.stepSummary: One view holds she would be embarrassed to ask for the missing דינר, so his promise was not kept and there is no קידושין. The other view holds she would not be embarrassed, so the קידושין works.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: it is embarrassing for her to ask for it. The other master holds: it is not embarrassing for her to ask for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's answer by explaining what each side of the ברייתא holds in the case of the missing דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is too embarrassed to ask, she will never get the full מנה, so he did not keep his word and she is not מקודשת. If she would ask, the missing דינר is just a debt he will pay back, so she is מקודשת. Either way, the argument has nothing to do with רב's rule about loans.

keyTerms.meaning: one master holds
embarrassing
to demand it, to claim it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not argue with רב. It argues about whether a woman would be too embarrassed to claim a missing דינר from the man she is marrying.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'loan' here is not a regular loan given before the קידושין. It is the missing דינר of the promised מנה.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: כְּסִיפָא לַהּ מִילְּתָא לְמִיתְבְּעֵיהּ.
phrases.english: One master holds: the matter is embarrassing for her, to demand it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא כְּסִיפָא לַהּ מִילְּתָא לְמִיתְבְּעֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: the matter is not embarrassing for her, to demand it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: כְּסִיפָא לַהּ מִילְּתָא לְמִיתְבְּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן's answer by explaining both opinions in his case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the dispute by a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about whether a loan is given to be spent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether she would be embarrassed to claim the missing דינר, and רב's rule stands.

steps.title: Does רבי אלעזר's ruling now depend on a dispute?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא's argument is about a promised מנה that came up one דינר short, then רבי אלעזר's ruling (she is מקודשת with one דינר, and he pays the rest later) seems to follow only one side of that argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רבי אלעזר's ruling? He said that if a man says 'Be מקודשת to me with a מנה' and gives her only one דינר, she is מקודשת and he must pay the rest. Should we say he holds like only one side of the תנאים' argument?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's reading of the ברייתא by pointing to a ruling of רבי אלעזר that now seems to fit only one side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, one תנא says that when part of the promised מנה is missing, there is no קידושין. רבי אלעזר says that even when most of the מנה is missing, she is מקודשת and he pays the rest later. So it looks like רבי אלעזר agrees only with the תנא who says the קידושין works.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money equal to one hundred דינרים
A coin; one hundredth of a מנה
And he must complete (pay the rest)
Like one side of a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: But then, that which Rabbi Elazar said:
"Be betrothed to me with a maneh"
and he gave her one dinar,
she is betrothed, and he must pay the rest;
shall we say he stated his teaching according to one side of the tannaim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב הונא's reading of the ברייתא (Steps 17-18) against a known ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading of the ברייתא as a dispute about a מנה that is short one דינר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a missing amount can cancel the קידושין according to one תנא, then רבי אלעזר's ruling that she is מקודשת with only one דינר given seems to fit only the other תנא. The גמרא prefers not to say a standard ruling depends on a dispute.

steps.title: Short by one דינר is not like short by ninety-nine
steps.stepSummary: The answer: when only one דינר is missing, she is embarrassed to ask for it. When ninety-nine are missing, she is not embarrassed to ask. So in רבי אלעזר's case, everyone agrees she is מקודשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: When the מנה is missing one דינר, she is embarrassed to ask for it. When it is missing ninety-nine, she is not embarrassed to ask for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רבי אלעזר's case is different from the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's dispute is only about a tiny shortfall, which she would feel too awkward to ask for, so the promise may never be kept. In רבי אלעזר's case he gave just one דינר out of a hundred, so she will easily ask for the rest. Both תנאים would agree that this קידושין works.

keyTerms.meaning: Missing, lacking
She is embarrassed
To demand it, to ask for it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's argument is only about a small shortfall that she would be too embarrassed to ask for. A big shortfall, like in רבי אלעזר's case, does not cancel the קידושין according to anyone.

phrases.english: They say:
A maneh missing one dinar:
the matter is embarrassing for her, so she won't demand it;
a maneh missing ninety-nine:
the matter is not embarrassing for her to demand it.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר's case: he gave only one דינר, so ninety-nine are still owed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מָנֶה חָסֵר דִּינָר כְּסִיפָא לַהּ מִילְּתָא לְמִיתְבְּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (small shortfall versus large shortfall)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ruling seemed to follow only the תנא who says a missing amount does not cancel the קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees with רבי אלעזר, because with ninety-nine missing she is not embarrassed to ask, so his promise will be fulfilled.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a loan works for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא. With a deposit, she is מקודשת only if a פרוטה's worth of it is still there. With a loan, she is מקודשת even if nothing is left. Then a second opinion begins: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: If a man says to a woman, 'Be מקודשת to me with the deposit I left with you,' and she finds that it was stolen or lost, then if a פרוטה's worth is left, she is מקודשת, and if not, she is not. But with a loan, even if not a פרוטה's worth is left, she is מקודשת. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: a loan…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב's rule (Step 14) that a loan cannot be used for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deposit still belongs to the man, so it works only if at least a פרוטה's worth actually exists. The ברייתא says a loan works even when nothing of it is left, which is the exact opposite of רב, who said a loan does not create קידושין. The ברייתא then begins a second opinion, from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, which continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit: something left with someone for safekeeping, which still belongs to the owner
A loan, given to be spent
The value of a פרוטה, the smallest amount that can create קידושין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the deposit and the loan. A deposit stays the man's, so it must still exist. A loan was hers to spend, and the ברייתא's first opinion says it works even when nothing of it is left.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who says to a woman:
"Be betrothed to me with the deposit that I have in your hand,"
and she went and found it
that it had been stolen or lost:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר הֵימֶנּוּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: if a peruta's worth of it remains, she is betrothed;
and if not, she is not betrothed.
But with a loan,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר הֵימֶנּוּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: even though not a peruta's worth of it remains, she is betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
A loan…

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשָּׁה הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְּפִקָּדוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּיָדֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the side discussion about רבי אלעזר, the גמרא returns to challenge רב's original ruling from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a loan cannot create קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's first opinion says a woman is מקודשת with a loan even when nothing of it is left, which directly contradicts רב.
